blocks.content: This chapter extends the vegetation contrast introduced in Chapter 2 into the UT's formal protected-area network and notable fauna — a smaller but still exam-relevant subject for this compact territory.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Protected areas in India are categorized under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 into National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Conservation Reserves, and Community Reserves.
National Parks offer the highest level of legal protection where no human activity, grazing, or private landholding is allowed.
Wildlife Sanctuaries permit limited human activities such as regulated livestock grazing and timber harvesting.
Major flagship species projects include Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant (1992), and Project Snow Leopard (2009).
Environmental concerns primarily encompass habitat fragmentation, human-wildlife conflict, biodiversity loss, and invasive alien species.

cells: The UT's principal wildlife sanctuary, protecting the dry/moist deciduous forest tract and its resident fauna

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Aviary at Jampore, Daman, is a genuinely recent (2020s) infrastructure project that has featured in Presidential and Vice-Presidential visit itineraries — a good example of how this UT's 'environment' chapter overlaps with current-affairs/schemes questions.

items: Dadra & Nagar Haveli's forest tracts support typical Western Ghats-foothill fauna — leopard, wild boar, jackal, various deer species, and a range of birdlife, reptiles and small mammals characteristic of dry/moist deciduous forest ecosystems.

Daman and Diu's coastal and marine environment supports fishing-economy-relevant marine life, migratory shorebirds at estuaries and mudflats, and — around Diu's rocky coast — occasional sightings of dolphins offshore.

The Daman Ganga river and its estuary support freshwater and estuarine fish species central to the local fishing economy in both Dadra & Nagar Haveli (upstream, freshwater) and Daman (downstream, estuarine/marine).
Wildlife Protection Act, 1972 forms the legal basis for declaring National Parks and Sanctuaries in India.
National Parks are created by state government notification, and boundaries cannot be altered except on recommendation of the National Board for Wildlife (NBWL).
Biosphere Reserves follow the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) program structure: Core Zone, Buffer Zone, and Transition Zone.

Rapid industrialisation in Dadra & Nagar Haveli has raised concerns about water pollution in the Daman Ganga and its tributaries from industrial effluent, prompting stricter Pollution Control Committee oversight in recent years.
Coastal erosion and encroachment pressure affect parts of the Daman and Diu shoreline, addressed partly through afforestation (casuarina belts) and coastal-zone regulation enforcement.

Groundwater stress in the industrialised Dadra & Nagar Haveli belt, driven by rapid population growth from migrant industrial labour, is an ongoing administrative concern flagged in local planning documents.
Nagar Haveli Wildlife Sanctuary is the UT's principal protected forest area.
Aviary at Jampore (Daman) — a notable recent bird-park/conservation project, visited by the President (Nov 2024) and Vice-President (Sept 2024).
Industrial pollution of the Daman Ganga is a key environmental concern linked to Dadra & Nagar Haveli's manufacturing growth.
